whys.why: Why was 'aspect 9:16' not met in D20a?
whys.because: The delivered file is landscape, 858x480 (16:9 at 480p), not 480x858.
whys.evidence: s3/s3.old.stupid.D20a/grade.json: check 'aspect 9:16' pass=false, got ["858x480"]. calls.jsonl, wait_for_video_project result: width 858, height 480. Passing chats (s3.old.happy.D20a, s3.old.dumper.D20a, s3.new.happy.D20a, s3.new.stupid.D20a) measured 480x858.

whys.because: The assistant itself asked for 16:9. The model returned exactly the ratio it was sent, so nothing went wrong in generation.
whys.evidence: s3.old.stupid.D20a/calls.jsonl: create_video_from_text args aspect_ratio "16:9", resolution 480p, end_seconds 10. The final reply says 'A 10-second, 16:9 video' and offers 'make it vertical (9:16) for Reels or TikTok' as a later change.

whys.because: The user's message never said vertical, Instagram or reel, so the assistant filled the gap with its own 16:9 default and did not ask.
whys.evidence: s3.old.stupid.D20a/chat.json: the only user message is 'make a café video from this pic this pic this pic this pic and this pic'. The words 'vertical', 'Instagram' and 'reel' from the D20a brief turn text are missing. The fact sits only in the persona's bank ('Vertical Instagram reel, 9:16, 10 seconds'), which the persona uses only to answer questions.

whys.why: Why did the shape fact get lost even when the assistant asked (new build)?
whys.because: The new build's planner made the assistant ask four questions at once, with shape second. The stupid persona answers only the first question it understands, so it said 'like 10 sec'. The assistant then re-planned with 16:9 and did not ask about shape again.
whys.evidence: s3.new.stupid.D20b/calls.jsonl: the first assistant 'say' asks 1. Length 2. Shape (16:9 / vertical 9:16 Reels/TikTok / 1:1) 3. Sound 4. Text. The user replies 'like 10 sec'. The second plan_video_production call still has story.aspect "16:9", and its checklist says 'One file, 10 s, 16:9'. chat.json persona rule: 'When it asks more than two things at once, answer only the first one you understand.'

whys.why: Why did the user message not contain 'vertical' in the first place?
whys.because: The harness rewrites the brief's opening line into the persona's vague style (stupid and probably dumper/happy variants), and that rewrite can drop the format words. The item marks asks:'never', which assumes the opening line already carries every fact. So the item expects no question, but the rewritten opener leaves the shape unknown.
whys.evidence: items/D20a.json: turns[0].text 'Make a 10-second vertical Instagram reel…', expect.asks 'never', spec.aspect '9:16'. s3.old.stupid.D20a/chat.json messages[0].text keeps neither 'vertical' nor 'Instagram'. Missing: I could not open the 6 failing happy chats (only s3 exists, and s3.old.happy.D20a passed), so I cannot confirm that their openers also lost the word. This is the best-supported cause, but it is unproven for happy users.

whys.why: Why does a lost shape word turn into 16:9 instead of a question or the right guess?
whys.because: Nothing in the tools makes the assistant check the shape. In the old build, aspect_ratio is a free argument with no guidance to ask about it. In the new build, the planner accepts whatever story.aspect the assistant sends and never flags 'shape not confirmed'. The assistant's own default for an unspecified video is wide 16:9. This is the axiom.
whys.evidence: Old: create_video_from_text was called directly with aspect_ratio '16:9' and no question. New: the plan_video_production outputs have empty 'problems' and 'advice' lists even after the user never answered the shape question (s3.new.stupid.D20b/calls.jsonl, second plan call).

result.axiom: When no shape reaches the assistant, it defaults to wide 16:9 for a video. The shape goes missing for two reasons. First, the harness persona's rewritten opener drops 'vertical Instagram reel' from the D20a brief, even though the item is marked asks:'never'. Second, if the assistant does ask, it asks in a multi-question batch, and the persona answers only the first question. No tool in either build checks that the shape was ever confirmed.
result.fix: Harness: when the persona rewrites an opener, keep the spec-critical facts (platform/shape 'vertical Instagram reel', length) for items with expect.asks='never', or drop those items' asks:'never' label for the stupid persona. Server (new build): in plan_video_production, add a 'problems' line when story.aspect was not stated by the user. Its 'how' text should tell the assistant to ask the shape alone, in plain words ('tall for Reels/TikTok, or wide?'), before any spend.
